recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit as-is. If the work group wants inline validation-limit wording on conformance-rules.html in the future, handle that as a fresh editorial issue rather than as a missed application of FHIR-7359.
issue_request: FHIR-7359 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-I change request against FHIR-core-conformance-rules. It objected to the note that none of the listed tools could check complete conformance and asked whether testing tools should check conformance to the FHIR specification and specific profiles; the resolution was to add a clarification note.
initial_application: SVN revision 6456, represented as git commit 4d589dd68bc9b557b73b073b069554ae4fbdeb92, replaced the local schema/validator/reference-platform list and blunt complete-conformance caveat with a link to validation.html for tools that assist with enforcing technical conformance to the base specification and profiles.
additional_context: Current conformance-rules.html remains an active top-level spec page linked from the conformance module and documentation index. Current validation.html lists profiles among validation aspects and states that validation methods are incomplete, limited to computable conformance, unable to check all narrative rules, and subordinate to human inspection. A later 2018 terminology-consistency commit removed the local phrase 'and profiles on it', but validation.html still covers profile validation, so the intended clarification was not lost. Zulip and Confluence searches found no contrary community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Repeating validation.html's caveat on the conformance rules page would be redundant and could create maintenance drift; the current link and validation guidance already answer the issue.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-7360 shared the 2015 conformance-rules implementation commit but concerns a separate isModifier clarification and is already represented on the combined branch.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking for clarification after the conformance page said no listed tools could check complete conformance.
evidence_items.learned: The final WG decision was to clarify validation and tooling expectations rather than require a complete-conformance testing tool.

evidence_items.summary: The active conformance rules page links to validation.html for tools that assist with enforcing technical conformance.
evidence_items.learned: The misleading local list and obsolete no-complete-conformance sentence are gone, and the page delegates tooling detail to validation.html.

evidence_items.summary: The validation page includes profile validation among validation aspects and states all validation methods are incomplete and limited to computable conformance.
evidence_items.learned: Current source already answers whether tools can check complete conformance to FHIR and profiles.

evidence_items.summary: 2015-08-21 commit '#7360 & #7359 - clarifications on conformance page' from SVN revision 6456 replaced the obsolete tool list and no-complete-conformance sentence.
evidence_items.learned: This matches the Jira application comment and shows how FHIR-7359 was originally applied.

evidence_items.learned: The current wording difference is explained by later cleanup and does not remove the profile-validation guidance from validation.html.
